| Android test IME                    | `AGENT_DEVICE_TEST_IME`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Public. Same setting as `--test-ime` / `--no-test-ime` on `open`, `test`, and `replay`; see known limitations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Local daemon storage                | `AGENT_DEVICE_STATE_DIR`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Public. The daemon and the CLI store the daemon’s record, lock, log, and recordings there, so the directory must belong to you alone: a real directory, not a symbolic link, that you own with mode `0700`, with every directory above it owned by you or root and not writable by group or other users (a shared directory that is sticky, like `/tmp`, is allowed). Every route that starts, attaches to, stops or reports on the daemon checks that first, before it reads or writes anything there. A missing directory is created at `0700` when a command starts a daemon, and is left missing when a command only reports. A directory you own that is open to the group or other users is closed to `0700` by that check, so a directory created by another program under a permissive umask, or left open by an older version, never stops the daemon. Anything else fails the check, with `details.reason: "daemon_state_root_unsafe"`, naming the directory and the step that ends it: `details.fix` runs `chmod 700` on that directory, or points `AGENT_DEVICE_STATE_DIR` at a real private directory you own, such as `$HOME/.agent-device`, when even that change is refused. For anything besides the mode bits it names that move, because a mode change cannot make a symbolic link, another owner’s directory, or a directory other accounts can write private. The check reads owner and mode bits and symbolic links, so it applies on macOS and Linux. On Windows agent-device only rejects a path shape it cannot support — a network path such as `\\server\share`, a device path such as `\\.\pipe\`, or a drive-relative path such as `C:state` — because there protection between accounts is not a question of mode bits, and a missing directory is still created when a command starts a daemon.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Recording helper cache              | `AGENT_DEVICE_SWIFT_CACHE_DIR`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Public operator control, read on macOS hosts. Recording compiles small Swift helpers and caches them here. The default is `~/Library/Caches/agent-device/swift-cache`. You or root must own the directory and every directory above it, and the group and other users must not have write access to any of them, even with the sticky bit set. A normal home directory at mode `0755` or `0750` is acceptable, and so are root-owned system directories such as `/Users`. A directory such as `/tmp` is refused. When the rule fails, recording refuses with `details.reason: "swift_cache_untrusted"`. The fix depends on which directory the refusal reports. For the cache root or a directory above it: if the group or other users can write to it, remove that access with `chmod g-w,o-w`; if another user owns it, or if it is a symbolic link, set this variable to a directory that only you can write. For `v3` or a directory inside it (`bin`, `home` and `module-cache`): agent-device creates these at mode `0700` and never deletes them, so if one of them is open to the group or other users, is a symbolic link, or is owned by another user, set this variable to a new directory that only you can write, or remove the reported directory yourself. Do not use `chmod` on it: that clears the refusal but keeps anything written while the directory was open. When recording compiles a Swift helper, it also checks the Xcode that `DEVELOPER_DIR` selects. A helper that is already compiled and cached is reused without checking that selection, so the same value can pass while the cache is warm and be refused when a helper next needs to compile. If that directory, or a directory above it, is owned by another user or open to the group or other users, recording refuses with `details.exposure: "untrusted_developer_dir"`. `/Applications` is the one exception, as stock macOS sets it up. A daemon keeps the `DEVELOPER_DIR` it started with, so unsetting it in your shell is not enough. To fix this, restart the daemon with `DEVELOPER_DIR` unset, or pass `DEVELOPER_DIR=''` to one local command to select the system default, or point it at an Xcode `Contents/Developer` directory, given as an absolute path, that you or root own along with every directory above it. agent-device checks only owner and mode bits, not ACLs. This applies to the default location and to an override. You must make sure that no ACL gives write access to another user. |
| Metro and install helpers           | `AGENT_DEVICE_METRO_BEARER_TOKEN`, `AGENT_DEVICE_BUNDLETOOL_JAR`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Public | App hooks and logs                  | `AGENT_DEVICE_APP_EVENT_URL_TEMPLATE`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_APP_EVENT_URL_TEMPLATE`, `AGENT_DEVICE_MACOS_APP_EVENT_URL_TEMPLATE`, `AGENT_DEVICE_ANDROID_APP_EVENT_URL_TEMPLATE`, `AGENT_DEVICE_APP_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, `AGENT_DEVICE_APP_LOG_MAX_FILES`, `AGENT_DEVICE_APP_LOG_REDACT_PATTERNS`, `AGENT_DEVICE_EVENT_LOG_MAX_BYTES` | Public. | Apple runner setup                  | `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_TEAM_ID`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_BUNDLE_ID`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_RUNNER_DERIVED_PATH`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_CLEAN_DERIVED`, `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_RUNNER_CACHE_KEEP`                                                                       | Public operator controls. A rebuild builds new products beside them. `AGENT_DEVICE_IOS_RUNNER_CACHE_KEEP` is the number of most-recent runner cache keys per platform folder (for example `ios-simulator` and `ios-device` are counted separately) guaranteed to survive a new build, the new key included (default 3, `0` keeps all). Keys used in the last day, held by a build, or named by a live runner lease also survive, so it is not a hard disk-usage cap.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

## Command-specific defaults

A command-specific key applies only to commands that support it, so one config file works across all commands. For example:

* A default `snapshotDepth` applies to `snapshot`, `diff snapshot`, `click`, `fill`, `get`, `wait`, `find`, and `is`.
* The same `snapshotDepth` value is ignored for commands like `open`, `close`, or `devices`.
* A default `screenshotScale` (or `AGENT_DEVICE_SCREENSHOT_SCALE`) applies to `screenshot`; an explicit `--scale` wins.

## When config fails to load

* If `--config` or `AGENT_DEVICE_CONFIG` points to a missing file, the command fails before it contacts the daemon.
* Invalid JSON, unknown keys, invalid values, or an operator-controlled key in project config also fail before the daemon is contacted, with `INVALID_ARGS`. The error names the key and never prints its value.

# Debugging and profiling

When UI automation is not enough, use these commands to collect runtime evidence from the app or device.

## What you can capture

* Session app logs for targeted debugging windows
* Network inspection from recent HTTP(s) entries in app logs via `network dump`
* Audio-level probes for browser media elements and host-rendered simulator/emulator audio
* Focused performance evidence with `perf frames`, `perf memory`, and native profile reports
* Apple crash symbolication with `debug symbols`
* Screenshots, recordings, and replayable repro flows

## React Native components

To see what React renders behind a screen, read the component tree and inspect a component:

```bash
agent-device react-devtools find ContactRow
agent-device react-devtools inspect @c42
agent-device react-devtools tree @c40 --depth 3
agent-device react-devtools errors
```

`find` and `tree` print `@c` refs. `inspect` shows the owners that rendered a component, its props, state, and hooks, and the errors and warnings it logged while rendering:

```text
@c42 ContactRow key=3
rendered by: ContactList @c40 < MemoDefeatedScenario @c38 < PerfLabScreen @c12
props:
  contact: {id: 3, name: "Ada Lovelace"}
  onSelect: ƒ onSelect() {}
hooks:
  State: false
```

`inspect` also takes a component name when only one mounted component has it. `errors` lists the components that logged console errors or warnings while rendering, with the messages; on older React Native versions, such as 0.74 and 0.76, it notes that the list can be incomplete. Refs change when a component remounts or the app reloads.

These commands use the same connection as profiling, described below. If a React DevTools window is connected to the app, close it and reload the app first.

## React Native performance profiling

To find out why an interaction renders slowly, record a React profile around it:

```bash
agent-device react-devtools profile start
agent-device fill 'id="catalog-search"' "tart" --delay-ms 100
agent-device react-devtools profile stop
```

`profile stop` saves the recording and prints a short diagnosis: how many commits React made, how long they took, how many went over the 16 ms frame budget (when any did), and the problems it found, worst first. If changed-prop inspection is interrupted after collection, you can still read the saved recording with `profile report` and `profile commit`. Each finding names a component, shows the evidence, and suggests a fix:

```text
React profile 8.3s: 8 commits, 1303ms rendering, 8 over 16ms (worst #6 188ms)
1. memo-defeated ContactRow: memo bypassed on 480/480 updates; new highlight (object) 480x, onSelect (function) 480x from ContactList -> wrap those props in useCallback/useMemo in ContactList
```

| Finding           | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `slow-render`     | The component’s own render is expensive.                                                        |
| `memo-defeated`   | A memoized component often re-renders because props change identity.                            |
| `parent-cascade`  | The component often re-renders with unchanged props, state, and context when its owner renders. |
| `context-cascade` | Most of the component’s renders come from context changes.                                      |
| `effect-chain`    | The component triggers a follow-up commit right after rendering, likely state set in an effect. |
| `render-storm`    | One component commits many times per second.                                                    |
| `eager-mount`     | Hundreds of instances of one component mount in a single commit.                                |
| `slow-commit`     | A commit took three frames or more, and other findings leave most of it unexplained.            |

To dig into a finding, use the saved profile:

```bash
agent-device react-devtools profile report ContactRow
agent-device react-devtools profile commit 6
agent-device react-devtools profile report
agent-device react-devtools profile commit
```

Without an argument, `report` lists components by self time with why they rendered, and `commit` lists the commits in order.

Profiling works with development builds of React Native 0.74 and later, including Expo, and is verified on Android emulators and iOS simulators. It connects to the app through the Metro dev server, so the app, Metro config, and Babel config need no changes. If several apps use the same dev server, pass `--app <bundle-id>`. If one app runs on several devices connected to the same dev server, pass `--metro-device <name>` with a device name the error lists. If the dev server is not the session’s Metro server or `localhost:8081`, pass `--metro-port` and `--metro-host`.

Development builds render slower than release builds. Compare profiles of the same interaction before and after a change rather than reading the numbers as absolute.

Component inspection and profiling also work through `agent-device proxy` and on remote bridge sessions, where they use the Metro server next to the agent: the session’s binding from `metro prepare`, or `--metro-host`/`--metro-port`. Metro accepts the debugger connection only from its own machine, so the bridge or `metroPublicBaseUrl` cannot carry it.

For React Native apps, overlays, Metro/Fast Refresh blockers, and routing to profiling or debugging evidence, start with `agent-device help react-native`. For slow-flow investigations, combine `help react-devtools` for the React profile with `help debugging` for log markers, network/audio evidence, traces, and perf samples.

React Native warning and error overlays come from the app. Treat them as findings or blockers: capture them, run `agent-device react-native dismiss-overlay` when the overlay is unrelated, then re-snapshot and report the overlay.

For permission prompts and other alerts already on screen, see [Wait and alerts](/docs/commands#wait-and-alerts).

## React Native JS memory through CDP

Use `cdp` when a React Native or Expo app exposes a Metro CDP target and you need JavaScript heap usage, heap snapshots, allocation hotspots, retained-object diffs, retaining paths, or a small runtime eval to confirm JS state.

```bash
agent-device cdp target list --url http://127.0.0.1:8081
agent-device cdp target select <target-id>
agent-device cdp memory usage sample --label baseline --gc
agent-device cdp memory snapshot capture --name baseline --gc
agent-device cdp memory snapshot diff --base ms_1 --compare ms_2 --limit 10
agent-device cdp memory snapshot leak-triplet --baseline ms_1 --action ms_2 --cleanup ms_3 --limit 10
agent-device cdp memory snapshot retainers --snapshot ms_3 --id <node-id> --depth 8 --limit 10
```

* `cdp` runs a pinned CDP helper through npm. The first run may download the package; later runs reuse the npm cache.
* Every argument after `cdp` is passed to the CDP helper. Put `agent-device` global flags before `cdp` when you need the outer CLI to consume them.
* In remote bridge sessions, run `connect` first and omit `--url` for `target list` or `target select`; `agent-device` derives the Metro CDP URL from the prepared remote runtime.
* Start with `memory usage sample --gc` for a quick JS heap growth signal. Use snapshot diff and `leak-triplet` for proof that objects stayed retained after cleanup.
* `cdp` has no single leak-report command. Build one from `memory usage diff`, `memory snapshot diff`, `memory snapshot leak-triplet`, and `memory snapshot retainers`.
* Keep raw heap snapshots and allocation exports as artifacts. Summarize heap deltas, top retained classes/shapes, leak-triplet rows that stayed high after cleanup, and shortest useful retaining paths.
* React Native/Hermes supports only part of browser CDP. If a method is unsupported, keep the selected target and fall back to heap usage samples plus heap snapshots.
* Prefer `perf cpu`, `trace`, `network`, `logs`, and `react-devtools` over `cdp profile cpu`, `trace`, `network`, and `console`.
* Use `perf memory sample` and `perf memory snapshot` for native/process memory. Use `cdp` only for JavaScript heap evidence.

## Capture a clean repro window

```bash
agent-device open MyApp --platform ios
agent-device logs clear --restart
agent-device logs mark "before repro"
agent-device press 'id="submit"'
agent-device network dump 25 --include headers
agent-device perf frames --json
agent-device perf memory sample --json
agent-device logs path
```

This flow gives you logs, recent network activity, and a quick metrics sample from the active app session, starting from an empty log.

`open` prints `Session state: <path>`. That directory holds the run’s request diagnostics, Apple runner output, and app logs; see [Find a session’s logs and artifacts](/docs/sessions#find-a-sessions-logs-and-artifacts).

When a command fails, stderr starts and ends with the same summary line, so the error stays visible when you keep only the first or the last line of output. Live progress and `--debug` output can print before the first copy, so `tail -1` or `--json` is the reliable way to read the error:

```text
Error (COMMAND_FAILED): tap @e12: runner did not answer within 10s. May have reached the device. Next: Run snapshot to check the screen before you retry. Read the diagnostics log for the failing step.
Log: /Users/me/.agent-device/sessions/<session>/requests/<request-id>.ndjson
Error (COMMAND_FAILED): tap @e12: runner did not answer within 10s. May have reached the device. Next: Run snapshot to check the screen before you retry. Read the diagnostics log for the failing step.
```

When agent-device knows whether the action reached the device, the summary says so. `May have reached the device` means the action can already have run, so check the screen before you retry it. `Not dispatched` means a retry is safe. A summary with neither does not prove that the action did not run. `Next` is the step to take. The `Log` line names the failing request’s diagnostics file.

Use `--json` to inspect `error.details.stderr` when it is present. Diagnostic stderr is secret-redacted and retains up to 8,192 characters; longer output keeps its beginning and end with a truncation marker between them. Other diagnostic strings remain limited to 400 characters. Compact retry summaries may retain less output.

When a command fails against a remote daemon, the `Log:` path is always on your machine: agent-device downloads the failing request’s record over the same base URL and token into `<state-dir>/remote-diagnostics/<session>/requests/<request-id>.ndjson`, so a CI job can keep it as a build artifact. If the download fails, the line reads `Log: unavailable` with the remote daemon, the request id, and the reason — never a path on the daemon host.

On iOS simulators, `logs` scope by bundle id and the resolved app executable. For launch-time stdout/stderr, capture the direct app launch console instead of starting raw `simctl` streams:

```bash
agent-device open MyApp --platform ios --relaunch --launch-console ./artifacts/app.console.log
```

`--launch-console` is only for direct app launches on local or Limrun iOS simulators, not URL opens.

## Crash symbolication

Pick the tool for what you need:

| Need                                                                          | Use             |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Lead-up timeline before a failure                                             | `logs`          |
| Failing frame from `crash.ips`/`crash.log` plus matching dSYM/build directory | `debug symbols` |
| Live state, breakpoints, variables, memory, or stepping                       | Xcode/LLDB      |

Use `debug symbols` when you already have an Apple crash artifact and local dSYMs and need the failing code path, not a full log dump:

```bash
agent-device debug symbols --artifact crash.log --dsym MyApp.dSYM --out crash-symbolicated.log
agent-device debug symbols --artifact crash.ips --search-path ./build --out crash-symbolicated.ips
```

The command supports Apple `.ips`, `.crash`, and log-style crash artifacts that contain Binary Images or IPS `usedImages`. It matches UUIDs from the crash artifact against `dwarfdump --uuid` output from `.dSYM` bundles, runs `atos`, writes a symbolicated artifact, and prints only the output path plus a compact crash report: app/thread, exception or termination, top symbolicated frames, and the first actionable frame finding. The full symbolicated artifact stays on disk, so agent context stays small.

`debug` covers symbolication only. Use `logs` for app logs, `network` for HTTP evidence, `perf` for performance samples, `record`/`trace` for media and traces, and `react-devtools` for React Native components and performance profiling. `debug symbols` does not handle Android Java/R8 `mapping.txt` or native `ndk-stack`/`addr2line` symbolication; capture Android crash evidence with `logs` and symbolicate it with other tools.

## Core commands

### Logs

```bash
agent-device logs start
agent-device logs stop
agent-device logs clear --restart
agent-device logs path
agent-device logs doctor
agent-device logs mark "before submit"
```

* Logging is off by default; turn it on only for focused debugging windows.
* Prefer `logs clear --restart` for clean repro loops.

#### Search app logs with grep

Run `logs path` to get the log file, then `grep` that path so only matching lines enter agent context:

```bash
# Prints the app log path, for example ~/.agent-device/sessions/default/app.log
agent-device logs path


# -n adds line numbers; -E allows | without escaping
grep -n "Error\|Exception\|Fatal" ~/.agent-device/sessions/default/app.log
grep -n -E "Error|Exception|Fatal|crash" ~/.agent-device/sessions/default/app.log
grep -n -E "agent-device.*mark|before submit" ~/.agent-device/sessions/default/app.log


# Last 50 lines only
tail -50 ~/.agent-device/sessions/default/app.log
```

* Replace the example path with the one `logs path` prints.
* Prefer targeted patterns (such as `Error`, `Exception`, or your own log tags) over reading the whole file.
* `logs mark "before submit"` writes a line prefixed with `[agent-device][mark][...]`, so grep for `agent-device.*mark` to find your timing markers.

### Network inspection

```bash
agent-device network dump 25
agent-device network dump 25 --include headers
agent-device network dump 25 --include all
```

* `network dump` parses recent HTTP(s) entries from the session app log for app/device sessions and from managed `agent-browser` request history for web sessions.
* For app/device sessions, results depend on what the app writes to the platform log.
* On Android, results include logcat timestamps, and status and duration can be filled in from adjacent GIBSDK packet lines when the URL is logged separately. Log streaming reattaches to the app’s new process after a restart.
* On iOS simulators, logs stream from inside the simulator, and `network dump` reads recent simulator log history when the live window is sparse.
* On iOS, `network dump` can return zero entries for real traffic when the app does not log request metadata to Unified Logging. The response notes tell an empty repro window apart from a log window with no network lines.
* On iOS, the system logs a request URL only when it opens a connection. Requests that reuse a keep-alive connection are reported against that connection’s origin with `pathUnavailable: true`, their status, and timing. Requests whose connection opened before the scanned window are only counted in `unnamedRequests`. Treat an endpoint missing from an iOS dump as unproven, not as never called.
* On web, request and response bodies are not available; use `agent-browser` HAR capture directly when you need them.
* On BrowserStack, AWS Device Farm, and TestMu AI sessions, `network dump` refuses with `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` and `details.reason: "network-capture-post-session"`. Those providers own the network path, so the session has no live source to read. Where the provider records traffic at all, it publishes the report on its own dashboard after its session ends. Limrun keeps live `network dump`. See [Device clouds](/docs/device-clouds).
* For the alias and scan limits, see [Media and logs](/docs/commands#media-and-logs).

### Audio probes

```bash
agent-device audio probe start 10 1000 --platform web
agent-device audio probe status --platform web
agent-device audio probe stop --platform web
agent-device audio probe start 10 1000 --platform macos
agent-device audio probe start 10 1000 --platform ios
agent-device audio probe start 10 1000 --platform android
```

* `audio probe start [durationSeconds] [bucketMs]` samples live audio while the session keeps running and reports compact `rmsDbfs` and `peakDbfs` buckets. The first timing positional is seconds; the second is milliseconds.
* On web, the probe samples HTML media elements through Web Audio. URL-backed media may be routed through the probe `AudioContext` while observed.
* On macOS hosts, the probe samples host system audio through ScreenCaptureKit for macOS sessions, iOS simulators, and Android emulators. It requires Screen Recording permission and is system-audio evidence, not app-instrumented audio. Physical iOS and Android devices are not supported.
* Use `status` to poll partial buckets during a 10-20 second observation window, and `stop` to end the probe early.

### Performance snapshots

```bash
agent-device perf frames --json
agent-device perf memory sample --json
agent-device perf memory snapshot --kind android-hprof --out app.hprof
agent-device perf memory snapshot --kind memgraph --out app.memgraph
agent-device perf cpu profile start --kind xctrace --template "Time Profiler" --out app.trace
agent-device perf cpu profile stop --kind xctrace --out app.trace
agent-device perf cpu profile report --kind xctrace --out app-profile.json
agent-device perf cpu profile start --kind simpleperf --out cpu.perf.data
agent-device perf cpu profile stop --kind simpleperf --out cpu.perf.data
agent-device perf cpu profile report --kind simpleperf --out cpu-report.json
agent-device perf trace start --kind perfetto --out app.perfetto-trace
agent-device perf trace stop --kind perfetto --out app.perfetto-trace
```

* Name a `frames`, `memory`, `cpu`, or `trace` area. Bare `perf`, `perf sample`, `perf metrics`, and `metrics` fail with an error that names the replacement.
* `perf frames` returns a focused frame/jank-health payload.
* `perf memory sample` returns a compact memory-only payload. Prefer it over raw `dumpsys`/`leaks` output for a first pass: arrays stay bounded and the top consumers are listed compactly.
* Example sample shape: `{"metrics":{"memory":{"available":true,"totalPssKb":562958,"totalRssKb":570304,"topConsumers":[{"name":"Dalvik Heap","pssKb":213456}]}}}`.
* `perf memory snapshot` escalates to file artifacts. Android supports Java HPROF capture for active app processes when the build/device allows heap dumping. iOS simulator and macOS app sessions support memgraph capture. On physical iOS devices, memgraph capture reports unavailable with a hint.
* Heap and memgraph artifacts are returned as paths plus compact metadata. Example default output: `Memory artifact (android-hprof): /tmp/app.hprof (42MB)`. They are not printed or embedded in JSON by default. Native allocation tracing (heapprofd) is not supported.
* `perf cpu profile ... --kind xctrace` collects an Apple native `.trace`; `report` aggregates every run, returns at most ten weighted top functions in JSON, and prints five. `perf trace ... --kind xctrace` keeps trace data as an artifact.
* On iOS simulators and macOS, process sampling and captures target the resolved app executable. Other running copies with the same executable name are excluded, including copies installed on another simulator.
* Android native profiling uses `perf cpu profile ... --kind simpleperf`; its report likewise returns at most ten top functions and prints five. Android native trace capture uses `perf trace ... --kind perfetto`. These commands require an active Android app session and return artifact paths/summaries instead of dumping profile or trace contents.
* Use the compact result as evidence. For example, a successful Perfetto stop may return `state: "stopped"`, `outPath: "/tmp/app.perfetto-trace"`, `sizeBytes: 5392410`, and `method: "adb-shell-perfetto"` while the 5.3 MB raw trace remains on disk as the artifact.
* Memory and Android frame-health availability depend on platform and whether the active session is bound to an app/package. HarmonyOS reports process RSS through HDC; CPU profiling, frame sampling, and memory-snapshot artifacts remain unavailable on the public HDC surface.
* `open` returns app startup duration as `startup`.
* On Android and supported Apple targets, use `metrics.fps.droppedFramePercent` for the health check and `metrics.fps.worstWindows` to line up jank clusters with logs, network activity, or recent actions.
* Android frame health comes from `dumpsys gfxinfo <package> framestats` and memory from `dumpsys meminfo <package>`. Apple frame health comes from the xctrace Animation Hitches template, and memory from process RSS. Memory values are in kilobytes.
* Android frame health resets after each successful `perf frames` read and after `open <app>`. For a focused window, run `perf frames`, perform the interaction, then run `perf frames` again.
* On physical iOS devices, `perf frames` records a short xctrace sample. Keep the device unlocked and connected, with the app in the foreground.
* After an Android URL or deep-link `open`, including Expo Go and dev-client shells, agent-device tries to detect the foreground package. If the session still has no package, package-bound metrics stay unavailable until you run `open <app>`.
* The Simpleperf report artifact keeps up to 50 parsed rows.
* Without `--json`, each perf area prints a compact summary.

## Where to go deeper

* Full command reference: [Commands](/docs/commands)
* Node.js observability APIs: [Node.js API](/docs/client-api)
* Session behavior and lifecycle: [Sessions](/docs/sessions)

# Device clouds

> Choose a hosted device provider for agent and CI workflows.

Use a device cloud or farm when an agent needs to drive a hosted mobile device without an interactive login. Pick the provider whose account and devices you use:

* [BrowserStack](/docs/browserstack): Android and iOS App Automate sessions over WebDriver.
* [AWS Device Farm](/docs/aws-device-farm): Android and iOS remote-access sessions through AWS.
* [TestMu AI](/docs/testmu): Android emulator, iOS simulator, and real-device sessions over WebDriver.
* [Limrun](/docs/limrun): direct iOS simulator and Android emulator instances.
* [Revyl](/docs/revyl): iOS simulators and Android emulators rented from Revyl’s execution API.

## Compare providers

|                         | BrowserStack                                                    | AWS Device Farm                                                                                                       | TestMu AI                                                                                        | Limrun                                                                                      | Revyl                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Devices                 | Android and iOS real devices                                    | Android and iOS real devices                                                                                          | Android emulators and iOS simulators by default; real devices with `--provider-device-type real` | Android emulators and iOS simulators                                                        | Android emulators and iOS simulators                                        |
| Ships as                | Built in                                                        | Built in; needs the AWS CLI                                                                                           | The `@agent-device/testmu` plugin                                                                | Built in                                                                                    | The `@agent-device/revyl` plugin                                            |
| Credentials             | `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`, `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY`              | The AWS CLI credential chain, such as `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `AWS_REGION` | `LT_USERNAME`, `LT_ACCESS_KEY`                                                                   | `LIMRUN_API_KEY` (optional `LIMRUN_REGION`), or `LIM_*_INSTANCE_*` for an existing instance | `REVYL_API_KEY` (optional `REVYL_API_URL` for another Revyl backend)        |
| Device allocated on     | `open`                                                          | `open`                                                                                                                | `open`                                                                                           | First device command, such as `install` or `open`                                           | First device command, such as `open`                                        |
| App source              | `--provider-app`: `bs://` reference, HTTP(S) URL, or local path | `--aws-app-arn` upload ARN; no install after allocation                                                               | `--provider-app`: `lt://` reference, HTTP(S) URL, or local path                                  | `install <id> <path-or-url>`, or `open <asset-name>` for an uploaded asset                  | `--provider-app`: a public HTTPS URL only, installed when the device starts |
| Artifacts after `close` | Video, Appium and device logs, dashboard and public links       | Video and log files, once AWS finalizes them                                                                          | Video, Appium, device, network, and command logs, screenshots, dashboard link                    | None                                                                                        | None                                                                        |
| Port reverse            | No; use BrowserStack Local                                      | No                                                                                                                    | No                                                                                               | Android over ADB; not on iOS                                                                | No; publish the app server at a public URL                                  |
| Live `network dump`     | No; the provider owns the network path                          | No; the provider owns the network path                                                                                | No; the provider owns the network path                                                           | Yes                                                                                         | No; the provider owns the network path                                      |

## Shared workflow

Every provider runs through the local `agent-device` daemon. `connect` checks your credentials and configuration, then saves non-secret connection state; it does not allocate a device. BrowserStack, AWS Device Farm, and TestMu AI allocate a hosted session on `open`. Limrun allocates an instance on the first device command, such as `install` or `open`. Revyl allocates a device on the first device command, usually `open`.

Every provider follows the same steps:

1. Put provider credentials in CI secrets or another non-interactive credential source.
2. Set `AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION` to a name for this agent or CI job.
3. Run `agent-device connect <provider>` with the provider selectors.
4. Follow the printed next command to install or open the app.
5. Run normal device commands, then `agent-device close` and `agent-device disconnect`.

Every command on a provider connection that takes a session must name it, with `AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION`, `--session <name>`, or a `session` in your config. A command that names none fails with `INVALID_ARGS` and `details.reason: "REMOTE_SESSION_REQUIRED"`, before it leases anything, instead of using the connection that another agent or job on the same machine saved last. This includes `connect` itself.

Each provider accepts only its own provider flags (`--provider-*` and `--aws-*`). A flag the provider does not use fails with `INVALID_ARGS` naming the flag, whether you pass it to `connect`, `client.leases.allocate()`, or a remote-config profile, so no setting is silently dropped.

The generated remote profiles are safe to store as non-secret configuration. They can include app IDs, ARNs, device names, OS versions, and labels, but never provider API keys, access keys, or AWS secret keys.

## Use a provider only through MCP

Run `agent-device connect <provider>` in the same effective state directory before you start `agent-device mcp`. MCP exposes device commands such as `open`, `snapshot`, `close`, and `artifacts`, but not provider `connect` or `disconnect`.

## Change credentials while the daemon runs

A running daemon keeps the BrowserStack, TestMu AI, Limrun, and Revyl credentials it started with. If your shell holds different ones, the first command that allocates a device, such as `open`, refuses before it creates a session. Run `agent-device daemon stop` with the same `--state-dir`, then rerun the command. A shell that sets none of the provider’s variables uses the daemon’s credentials.

AWS Device Farm reads the AWS CLI credential chain instead, so this check does not apply to it.

## Fill text on hosted WebDriver sessions

On BrowserStack, AWS Device Farm, and TestMu AI, `fill` replaces existing text after it confirms which element received focus. It clears and sends replacement text to that same element. An empty replacement clears the field without sending keys. If clearing fails, no replacement text is sent.

Use `snapshot -i` to confirm the target. If the driver does not support the `/element/active` route, `fill` refuses before tapping. Keyboard visibility alone cannot identify the element to clear. `type` remains append-only. Use `press <target>` followed by `type <text>` only when you want to append text without confirming where it lands.

## Retrieve artifacts after close

After `close`, run `agent-device artifacts --json` to check for the artifacts your provider makes available (see [Compare providers](#compare-providers)). To look up an earlier session, pass its provider session ID:

```bash
agent-device artifacts <provider-session-id> --provider <provider> --json
```

Providers finalize video and log URLs after the session ends. If the lookup reports artifacts as pending right after `close`, retry it a little later.

## NoMac

[NoMac](https://nomac.app) runs hosted iPhone and iPad simulators. Its provider is the [`@nomac/agent-device`](https://github.com/NoMac-app/agent-device-plugin) plugin, which NoMac maintains. Install the plugin, then connect with a NoMac API key:

```bash
agent-device plugins add @nomac/agent-device
export NOMAC_API_KEY=...
export AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION=checkout-ios
agent-device connect nomac
```

For the devices, app installation, and supported commands, see the plugin’s [README](https://github.com/NoMac-app/agent-device-plugin#readme). Report plugin problems in [its repository](https://github.com/NoMac-app/agent-device-plugin/issues).

## Expo Simulators

[Expo Simulators](https://docs.expo.dev/preview/simulators/introduction/) runs Android Emulators and iOS Simulators on EAS. It is not an `agent-device` provider: an Expo Simulators session provisions its own `agent-device` daemon, and you run the same commands inside the session through `eas simulator:exec`:

```bash
eas simulator:exec npx agent-device@latest open com.example.app --platform ios
eas simulator:exec npx agent-device@latest snapshot -i
```

Expo Simulators is a limited-access preview. For session setup, see Expo’s [agent-device guide](https://docs.expo.dev/agents/agent-device/) and [Drive the device](https://docs.expo.dev/preview/simulators/how-to/drive-the-device/).

# Error reasons

> Every typed error.details.reason value that agent-device declares in a reason table, grouped by command and subsystem.

A failed command can name why it failed in `error.details.reason`. Branch on the reason, not on the message: a message can change, and a published reason keeps its spelling.

Treat a reason that this page does not list as unknown, not as an error in the response: a newer daemon or a provider plugin can add reasons. [Commands](/docs/commands) documents more reasons with the behavior of each command.

## Commands

### `alert`

| Reason                       | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `alert-not-found`            | No alert was visible to `alert accept` or `alert dismiss`, from the tree-based driver or the macOS helper, so nothing was pressed. Retry once the alert shows, or inspect `snapshot -i`. |
| `alert-wait-timeout`         | `alert wait` saw no actionable alert within its window.                                                                                                                                  |
| `alert_button_undecided`     | The sheet’s buttons name no single choice for the asked-for action.                                                                                                                      |
| `alert_capture_undecided`    | The capture is alert-shaped but resolves to no single alert.                                                                                                                             |
| `alert-window-expired`       | A press went out but the confirm window never settled whether the alert is gone.                                                                                                         |
| `alert-wait-window-too-long` | `alert wait` was given a longer window than it can honour; the command refuses it before running and never shortens it. `details.maxWaitWindowMs` names the limit.                       |

### `audit`

| Reason                          | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `native_audit_blocked_by_alert` | Apple’s audit failed while a system alert covered the app; answer the alert, then retry. |
| `native-audit-invalid-result`   | The runner answered the native audit with a missing or malformed result.                 |

### `auth`

| Reason                           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cli_session_revoked`            | The cloud answered a refresh by reporting the stored session revoked.                                                                                                                                                |
| `cli_session_refresh_unanswered` | The refresh answered without an access token, so the CLI has nothing to send.                                                                                                                                        |
| `cli_session_store_unwritable`   | The directory holding the session file cannot be written, so its lock cannot be taken.                                                                                                                               |
| `cloud_login_origin_mismatch`    | The cloud API origin named by AGENT\_DEVICE\_CLOUD\_BASE\_URL differs from the origin that issued the stored CLI session, so the stored credential is not sent. Log in with the named origin, or unset the override. |
| `cli_session_issuer_unverified`  | The stored CLI session does not record the cloud that issued its credential, as a session saved by an older CLI does not, so the credential is not sent. Run agent-device auth login.                                |
| `cloud_auth_redirect_refused`    | A cloud auth request got a redirect it does not follow: to another origin, past the third hop, or to a missing Location or one with a username or password. Nothing was sent to the target.                          |

### `back`

| Reason                            | Meaning                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `back_swipe_no_change`            | The back swipe ran and left the app’s screen unchanged.                                     |
| `back_swipe_unverified`           | The back swipe ran, but the screen was already changing or could not be sampled afterwards. |
| `back_swipe_not_dispatched`       | The back swipe was refused before it reached the device.                                    |
| `in_app_back_control_unavailable` | On macOS, the app’s accessibility tree exposes no in-app back control.                      |

### `batch`

| Reason                                   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fill_text_stdin_in_batch`               | A batch step asked `fill` to read its text from stdin, which a step does not have. Run that fill on its own with `--text-stdin`.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `bounded_composite_resource_unsupported` | The composite refused this step before dispatch because it must run as its own command, such as a recording, trace, log, audio or perf capture. `details.shape` names the refused operation or option, and `details.standaloneCommandName` the public command to run instead. Earlier steps may have run. |

### `clipboard`

| Reason                                        | Meaning                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `android_clipboard_shell_command_unavailable` | This Android build ships no shell command for the clipboard service. |

### `close`

| Reason                                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app-device-scope`                    | This session drives one macOS app as its own device, so it cannot open or close another app or open a surface other than `app`. Open another app in a separate `--session`. A whole-Mac surface such as `--surface desktop` opens only after the sessions holding app devices on that Mac end. |
| `android-app-close-timeout`           | A stop fence ended before the app left the foreground or its killed processes exited.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `android-process-probe-unavailable`   | `adb pidof` or the resumed-activity read did not answer, so process state is unknown.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `MACOS_APP_TERMINATION_TIMEOUT`       | The macOS app was still running after every termination attempt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `android_test_ime_restore_incomplete` | The IME could not be restored, so the device may still send test-helper text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### `connect`

| Reason                           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cli_session_revoked`            | The cloud answered a refresh by reporting the stored session revoked.                                                                                                                                                |
| `cli_session_refresh_unanswered` | The refresh answered without an access token, so the CLI has nothing to send.                                                                                                                                        |
| `cli_session_store_unwritable`   | The directory holding the session file cannot be written, so its lock cannot be taken.                                                                                                                               |
| `cloud_login_origin_mismatch`    | The cloud API origin named by AGENT\_DEVICE\_CLOUD\_BASE\_URL differs from the origin that issued the stored CLI session, so the stored credential is not sent. Log in with the named origin, or unset the override. |
| `cli_session_issuer_unverified`  | The stored CLI session does not record the cloud that issued its credential, as a session saved by an older CLI does not, so the credential is not sent. Run agent-device auth login.                                |
| `cloud_auth_redirect_refused`    | A cloud auth request got a redirect it does not follow: to another origin, past the third hop, or to a missing Location or one with a username or password. Nothing was sent to the target.                          |
| `plugin-unavailable`             | The provider’s plugin is present but cannot serve the provider; `details.failedPlugins` names what broke.                                                                                                            |
| `plugin-not-installed`           | No plugin declares this provider; `details.installCommand` is the command that adds it.                                                                                                                              |

### `events`

| Reason                        | Meaning                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `EVENT_LOG_CURSOR_EXPIRED`    | The cursor names a line that rotation has already removed from the retained window.                                       |
| `EVENT_LOG_WINDOW_UNVERIFIED` | The retained event log files or their window sidecar are malformed, incomplete, or disagree, so no cursor can be trusted. |

### `fill`

| Reason                                      | Meaning                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no_text_input_at_point`                    | A coordinate `fill` point identified no text input, so nothing was tapped or typed.                                             |
| `text_input_probe_unavailable`              | The runner could not tell whether a coordinate `fill` point holds a text input; nothing was tapped.                             |
| `fill_text_stdin_target_invalid`            | The stdin text mode’s positional list does not decode to exactly one target.                                                    |
| `fill_text_source_conflict`                 | The stdin text mode was also given a text argument, so the two sources disagree.                                                |
| `android_shell_text_unsupported`            | The adb-shell fallback carries ASCII text only; a helper or provider channel is needed.                                         |
| `android_ime_helper_no_ack`                 | The test IME helper gave no evidence it attempted the dispatch, so nothing is proven typed.                                     |
| `android_ime_helper_dispatch_rejected`      | The test IME helper answered that it rejected the dispatch, so nothing was typed.                                               |
| `fill_record_as_requires_armed_recording`   | `fill --record-as` needs an armed script recording; open a session with `--save-script` first.                                  |
| `fill_text_stdin_unparameterized_recording` | `fill --text-stdin` needs `--record-as` or `--no-record` while a recording is armed, so the stdin text stays out of the script. |
| `android_test_ime_rebind_unconfirmed`       | The test IME rebind could not be confirmed, so the focused field may have no input session.                                     |
| `fill_target_missing`                       | Only the text arrived: one value that is no target, or a blank target before the text.                                          |
| `fill_text_stdin_tty`                       | stdin is a terminal, so the command would wait for input no one is piping.                                                      |
| `fill_text_stdin_too_large`                 | The piped input passed the byte limit of 64 KiB.                                                                                |
| `fill_text_stdin_empty`                     | The piped input decoded to an empty string.                                                                                     |
| `fill_text_stdin_invalid_utf8`              | The piped input is not valid UTF-8, a lone surrogate included.                                                                  |

### `find`

| Reason                     | Meaning                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `find_snapshot_unreadable` | The capture came back sparse, so no selector could be resolved against it. |

### `fold`

| Reason                            | Meaning                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `single-panel-device`             | The device has one panel and no hinge, so there is no pose to set.                                                |
| `fold-pose-unverified`            | The pose was sent, but the device still reports another pose.                                                     |
| `fold-posture-unsupported`        | The emulator profile has no device state for the requested pose; `details.supportedPoses` lists the poses it has. |
| `fold-keyframes-unsupported`      | Android poses fixed postures only, so fold keyframes are refused.                                                 |
| `fold-posture-dispatch-failed`    | The Android emulator console refused the posture command.                                                         |
| `fold-lock-screen-persists`       | The lock screen that folding raised on Android did not stay dismissed.                                            |
| `fold-hinge-angle-unreadable`     | The Android emulator console returned no hinge angle.                                                             |
| `fold-helper-build-failed`        | The iOS simulator fold helper could not be built with the selected Xcode.                                         |
| `fold-hid-dispatch-failed`        | The fold helper could not send the hinge pose to the iOS simulator.                                               |
| `fold-hinge-angle-no-sample`      | An iOS simulator hinge read returned no usable sample; `details` say why.                                         |
| `fold-pose-dispatched-unverified` | The iOS simulator received the pose, but the first hinge read returned no sample to verify it.                    |
| `fold-angle-unverified`           | The iOS simulator hinge did not reach the angle of the final keyframe.                                            |
| `fold-pose-unsettled`             | The iOS simulator hinge reached the pose but never came to rest.                                                  |

### `gesture`

| Reason                             | Meaning                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `drag_endpoint_is_coordinates`     | A gesture drag endpoint is a number or an “x y” point; drag takes a ref or a selector.      |
| `GESTURE_TAP_DUPLICATE_POINT`      | Two tap contacts share coordinates, so one contact would press where another already rests. |
| `GESTURE_PATH_TOO_SHORT`           | The gesture path has fewer usable samples than any recognizable motion needs.               |
| `GESTURE_PATH_INVALID_TIMELINE`    | The path’s sample timeline is not ordered and finite, so no clock can play it back.         |
| `GESTURE_TRAJECTORY_NON_FINITE`    | A trajectory sample carries a non-finite coordinate.                                        |
| `GESTURE_TRAJECTORY_OUT_OF_BOUNDS` | A trajectory sample leaves the viewport, so the contact would press outside the screen.     |

### `install-from-source`

| Reason                                     | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ARTIFACT_BYTE_LIMIT`                      | The response declared or carried more bytes than the artifact budget allows.             |
| `source_materialization_deadline_exceeded` | The aggregate or handed-down materialization budget ran out before the source was ready. |

### `keyboard`

| Reason                         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `keyboard_dismiss_unavailable` | The keyboard stayed up: the Apple runner leaves a visible keyboard alone and presses nothing, or the Android IME stayed visible after Escape key events, which may have reached the app. `details.dispatched` says which. |

### `logs`

| Reason                                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `simulator-log-stream-launch-timeout` | The simulator log stream did not start in time.                                                                                                            |
| `app_log_redact_pattern_invalid`      | A redaction pattern in `AGENT_DEVICE_APP_LOG_REDACT_PATTERNS` does not compile; `details.patternIndex` names the field and the pattern text is not echoed. |

### `open`

| Reason                                   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `launch-console-owner-unadmitted`        | –launch-console was asked for on an app-launch owner that cannot stream a console.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `app-device-scope`                       | This session drives one macOS app as its own device, so it cannot open or close another app or open a surface other than `app`. Open another app in a separate `--session`. A whole-Mac surface such as `--surface desktop` opens only after the sessions holding app devices on that Mac end. |
| `claim-lost-during-open`                 | The device lost the claim this open was made with; close the session and open the device again.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `runtime-hints-operation-missing`        | Runtime hints were requested, but the device runtime admitted no operation to apply or clear them.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `android_port_reverse_rebind_refused`    | The endpoint already has a device mapping, which a `--no-rebind` reverse never replaces.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `invalid-android-activity-component`     | The `--activity` value is not an Android component name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `android-launch-not-foreground`          | The app the helper launched never reached the foreground before the launch budget ran out.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `android-app-close-timeout`              | A stop fence ended before the app left the foreground or its killed processes exited.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `android-process-probe-unavailable`      | `adb pidof` or the resumed-activity read did not answer, so process state is unknown.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ios-simulator-openurl-timeout`          | CoreSimulator did not answer `simctl openurl` in time, so the URL open failed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `system-surface-host-not-openable`       | The bundle hosts an iOS system surface, which `open` refuses to launch as an app.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `launch_confirmation_foreign_app`        | iOS asks to open another app’s URL scheme instead of the session app’s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `launch_confirmation_unanswered`         | The Simulator has not completed the launch URL; an “Open in” prompt may still be waiting.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `invalid-harmony-ability-name`           | –activity is not an ability name the module.json5 format can carry.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `open-not-foreground`                    | The launch was refused (a locked screen) or the poll answered without the app.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `open-foreground-probe-unreadable`       | The poll’s every read failed, so the foreground question stayed unanswered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `android_test_ime_recovery_fence_failed` | The recovery records that keep the IME switch safe could not be persisted, so the switch stays unsafe.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `foreground_app_ambiguous`               | `open --foreground` found no single running app to bring forward on the selected simulator.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### `orientation`

| Reason                                | Meaning                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fold-helper-build-failed`            | The iOS simulator fold helper could not be built with the selected Xcode.                         |
| `orientation-hid-dispatch-failed`     | The fold helper could not send the orientation to the iOS simulator.                              |

| `orientation-panel-table-unavailable` | The foldable’s guest panel table could not be read.                                               |

### `plugins`

| Reason                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `duplicate_provider`  | Two plugins claim one provider id, or a plugin claims an id that routing or a built-in provider owns.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `incompatible_plugin` | The package exports no plugin entry or declares no provider contract this build can load.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `plugin_load_failed`  | The plugin’s manifest or code could not be read, resolved, or loaded.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `plugin_setup_failed` | The plugin’s `setup(host)` threw, or registering what it returned failed.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `reserved_provider`   | A plugin claims a provider id reserved for daemon routing, `cloud` or `proxy`.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `invalid_plugin`      | The plugin package or what its code returns breaks the plugin contract: an invalid manifest, package version, provider id, credentials or connection, no default factory or `setup(host)`, or a runtime or WebDriver descriptor that lacks a required field. |

### `prepare`

| Reason                             | Meaning                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prepare_deadline_expired`         | `prepare ios-runner` ran out of its deadline before the named `details.phase` began.                                       |
| `prepare_rebuilt_runner_unhealthy` | The cached runner failed its health check, and the rebuilt runner failed it too; `details.rebuiltFailureMessage` says how. |

### `press`

| `sequence-replay-guard-unsupported` | A multi-ref press sequence cannot carry a replay target guard; re-record one press per key.     |

| `transfer_gateway_status`               | The upstream daemon answered with a status that is not an HTTP response this proxy may relay. |
| `transfer_upstream_closed`              | The upstream daemon closed the connection before it answered, or during a write.              |
