* The TV in Developer Mode and registered with `ares-setup-device`. To set this up, follow LG’s [App Testing with Developer Mode App](https://webostv.developer.lge.com/develop/getting-started/developer-mode-app). The name you give the TV there is the `--device` value for `connect`.
* The app installed on the TV.
* The TV and this host on the same network.

## Install the plugin

```bash
agent-device plugins add @agent-device/webos
```

The plugin is an optional npm package installed under `AGENT_DEVICE_HOME`. After you add or update it, close open sessions and run `agent-device daemon stop` with the state directory you use; the next device command loads the plugin.

Plugin options, set under `plugins["@agent-device/webos"].options` in `config.json`:

| Option    | Meaning                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `aresBin` | Directory with the `ares-*` CLIs, when they are not on `PATH` (for example a project’s `node_modules/.bin`). |
| `device`  | `ares-setup-device` entry to drive when `connect` names none. Defaults to the ares default device.           |

## Connect and run a session

```bash
export AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION=checkout-tv
agent-device connect webos --device living-room
agent-device open com.example.app
agent-device tv-remote press down
agent-device snapshot -i
agent-device screenshot ./tv.png
agent-device logs start
agent-device close com.example.app
agent-device disconnect
```

The TV is a leased device, so every command from `connect` to `disconnect` names its session with `AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION`, `--session <name>`, or a config session. Without one, the command fails with `REMOTE_SESSION_REQUIRED`.

`--device` names an `ares-setup-device` entry. Without it, the plugin uses the `device` option, then the ares default device. `connect` does not contact the TV; the plugin reads the TV from `ares-setup-device` when `open` starts the session.

agent-device leases only iOS, Android, and HarmonyOS devices, so a webOS TV enters as an Android TV device that the plugin owns (`platform: android`, `target: tv`, id `webos:<TV ip>:<port>`, or `webos:<ares device>` for a USB entry). Every command on that device goes to the plugin, never to adb.

## How commands map to the TV

| Command                                                                             | How                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open` / `close`                                                                    | `ares-launch` / `ares-launch --close`, then the `ares-inspect` tunnel                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `tv-remote press up/down/left/right/select/back`, `back`                            | `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` with the LG remote codes                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `tv-remote press media-play/media-pause/media-stop/media-rewind/media-fast-forward` | `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` with the LG media key codes                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `appstate`                                                                          | The attached app while its page is visible                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `apps`                                                                              | `ares-install --listfull`                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `logs`                                                                              | Console calls, exceptions, and browser log entries of the attached page, one line each                                                                                                                                                         |
| `snapshot`, `find`, `is`, `get`, `wait`                                             | A DOM walk over `Runtime.evaluate`: visible interactive, labelled, or text nodes, with focus from `document.activeElement`. `-s`, `-d`, and `-i` apply to the walk. A control whose centre hit-tests to another element is marked `[covered]`. |
| `screenshot`                                                                        | `Page.captureScreenshot`. `--crop-on <selector>` crops the capture to the frame of the node that the selector resolves in a snapshot taken on the same screen.                                                                                 |
| `click`, `press <x> <y>`, `longpress`, `hover`                                      | `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, the Magic Remote pointer                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `fill`                                                                              | Pointer press on the field, select its contents, then `Input.insertText`, or Backspace for an empty value                                                                                                                                      |
| `type`                                                                              | `Input.insertText` into the focused element                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `scroll`                                                                            | `mouseWheel` at the centre of the scroll container or the viewport, by the requested distance                                                                                                                                                  |

Not supported yet: system buttons (`home`, menu, volume, and channel), `media-play-pause`, `media-next` and `media-previous`, `network dump`, `perf`, `install` and `uninstall`, recording, URLs and deep links in `open`, and `power`. webOS has separate Play and Pause key codes and no play-pause toggle, so `media-play-pause` is refused; use `media-play` or `media-pause`.

## Known limitations

* Idle leases expire after 60 seconds by default, and expiry ends the session. When the lease ends, by `disconnect` or by expiry, the plugin closes the page connection and the `ares-inspect` tunnel. The next command then fails with `Lease is not active` or `No active session` and needs a new `connect` and `open`. To keep longer pauses alive, run `agent-device daemon stop`, export `AGENT_DEVICE_LEASE_TTL_MS` and `AGENT_DEVICE_LEASE_MAX_TTL_MS` (for example `1800000`), and run the next command in that shell. That command starts the daemon with both values.
* `screenshot` captures the app page, not the TV screen. When the app is in the background, for example after Home on the remote, the page is hidden and renders no frames, so `screenshot` fails; `open <appId>` brings the app back. System layers such as the LG menu and the on-screen keyboard never appear in `screenshot` or `snapshot`.
* Console messages logged before the attach are replayed without object previews.
* `open` on a running app can reload it. `open` waits for a loaded document; `open --relaunch` closes the app first for a cold start.
* A second DevTools client on the same page can hang the session. Close Chrome DevTools and other inspector clients attached to the app first.
* Snapshots are read from the DOM. Labels come from `aria-label`, `alt`, `title`, or own text. Rects are CSS pixels, and the screenshot holds the page at CSS pixels whatever its `devicePixelRatio`: on a 1920x1080 TV, an app at `"resolution": "1280x720"` reports 1.5 yet fills only the top-left 1280x720 of the capture. `screenshot --crop-on` scales rects by the page’s `visualViewport.scale`, which is 1 because webOS ignores the meta viewport, and clips the crop to the page. It refuses a page whose browser has no `visualViewport` or whose visual viewport is panned. `screenshot --overlay-refs` draws ref boxes at the same scale and stops them at the page edge. The walk does not enter iframes or shadow roots.
* `click`, `press`, `fill`, and `focus` refuse a control marked `[covered]`, because a tap at its centre would land on the element on top, such as a card’s own pressable area. `snapshot -i` still lists it, and `tv-remote` reaches it through focus.
